```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
.input <- normalizePath(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), mustWork = TRUE)
.root <- normalizePath(file.path(dirname(.input), ".."), mustWork = TRUE)
# Load the permutation engine and supplied-data interface together.
.workflow <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
for (.file in c("simulation_core.R", "kyfan_test.R")) {
  source(file.path(.root, "R", .file), local = .workflow)
}
```

# Supply two samples

Use two CSV files or two numeric R matrices/data frames. Rows are independent
observations; columns are measurements of the same variables in the same order.
Both groups must have the same sample size $m\geq2$ and dimension $p\geq1$.
Remove identifier and group-label columns before testing. Missing, infinite, or
nonnumeric measurements are rejected; no rows are silently removed.

For CSV input, edit `x_csv` and `y_csv` above and click **Knit**, or run the first
example below from the repository root. Relative paths resolve from that root.
CSV headers must match; set `csv_header: false` for files without a header.
For R objects, use the second example. Supply only one input mode.

```{r usage, eval=FALSE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/kyfan_data_test.Rmd",
  params = list(x_csv = "/path/group_x.csv", y_csv = "/path/group_y.csv",
                k = 1, B = 1000)
)

# Pass existing numeric samples; each row is one observation.
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/kyfan_data_test.Rmd",
  params = list(X = X_data, Y = Y_data, k = c(1, 3), B = 1000)
)
```

Choose $k$ before inspecting the data. The default is $k=1$; multiple specified
orders produce separate, unadjusted p-values using the same permutations.
The report does not select an order or combine tests.

# Statistic and p-value

Let $S_X$ and $S_Y$ be the sample covariance matrices, each computed using its own
sample mean and denominator $m-1$. The report returns both the unscaled Ky–Fan norm
and the statistic used in the manuscript:

$$
\|S_X-S_Y\|_{(k)}=\sum_{j=1}^k s_j(S_X-S_Y),
\qquad
Z_{m,k}=\sqrt m\,\|S_X-S_Y\|_{(k)},
$$

where $s_j$ are the singular values in decreasing order. For this symmetric
matrix, they are the absolute eigenvalues in decreasing order.

Each of $B=1000$ independent random reallocations assigns $m$ pooled observations
to one group and the remainder to the other. Group means and covariances are
recomputed each time. The upper-tail plus-one p-value is

$$
\widehat p_k=\frac{1+\sum_{b=1}^{B}
\mathbf 1\{Z_{m,k}^{\pi_b}\geq Z_{m,k}\}}{B+1}.
$$

Numerical ties are included using a tolerance of
$100\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{machine}}|Z_{m,k}|$ in the comparison.
The smallest possible reported p-value is $1/(B+1)$, approximately $0.001$ at
$B=1000$. Set `seed` to reproduce the sampled reallocations.

The manuscript assumes independent samples with a common population mean.
Under equal covariance but potentially different population distributions,
validity is asymptotic under its stated conditions. Finite-sample permutation
validity requires exchangeability. Matching or differing sample means alone
does not establish whether these assumptions hold.

# Results

```{r test}
# With no input, render the guide without running a test.
has_input <- !is.null(params$X) || !is.null(params$Y) ||
  nzchar(params$x_csv) || nzchar(params$y_csv)
fit <- NULL
if (has_input) {
  samples <- .workflow$kyfan_read_samples(
    X = params$X, Y = params$Y,
    x_csv = params$x_csv, y_csv = params$y_csv, root = .root,
    csv_header = params$csv_header, csv_sep = params$csv_sep
  )
  fit <- .workflow$method_kyfan(
    samples$X, samples$Y, k = params$k, B = params$B,
    seed = params$seed, alpha = params$alpha
  )
  knitr::kable(
    fit$summary[c("k", "kyfan_norm", "statistic", "exceedances", "p_value", "reject")],
    digits = 6,
    caption = sprintf("m = %d, p = %d, B = %d, alpha = %g",
                      nrow(samples$X), ncol(samples$X), fit$B, fit$alpha)
  )
} else {
  cat("No data supplied. Set both CSV paths or supply X and Y, then render again.\n")
}
```

`kyfan_norm` is the unscaled norm; `statistic` is $Z_{m,k}$.
`exceedances` counts simulated statistics at least as large as the observed
statistic, including numerical ties. `reject` records whether the p-value is
at most `alpha`, which defaults to 0.05.

```{r save-results}
if (!is.null(fit) && nzchar(params$output_dir)) {
  output_root <- path.expand(params$output_dir)
  if (!grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:[/\\\\])", output_root)) {
    output_root <- file.path(.root, output_root)
  }
  dir.create(output_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  # Create a new directory so earlier results are retained.
  result_dir <- tempfile("kyfan_", tmpdir = output_root)
  if (!dir.create(result_dir)) stop("Could not create the result directory.")
  write.csv(fit$summary, file.path(result_dir, "test_result.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(fit$permutation_statistics,
            file.path(result_dir, "permutation_statistics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  saveRDS(fit[c("B", "k", "seed", "alpha", "relative_tolerance")],
          file.path(result_dir, "configuration.rds"))
  writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), file.path(result_dir, "session_info.txt"))
  cat("Saved results:", normalizePath(result_dir), "\n")
}
```

Each run saves result and permutation-statistic CSVs in a new subdirectory of
`results/data_test/`, together with the configuration and R session information.
Input observations are not copied. Set `output_dir: ""` to skip these exports.

The numerical engine is shared with the simulations in `R/simulation_core.R`;
`R/kyfan_test.R` provides the supplied-data interface and numerical tie handling.
